Opposite Parties
 Mr. P.K. Sahoo, Asc
 Mr. A.Mohanta, Advocate for O.P.No.4
 Coram:
Mr. Justice R.K. Pattanaik

Order
19.11.2025 Order No.
05. 1.
Heard Mr. Bose, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel for opposite party No.4 besides Mr. Sahoo, learned ASC for the State.

2. Instant writ petition is filed by the petitioner to direct opposite party Nos. 2 to 4 to renew the agreement i.e. Annexure-1 and not to disturb his physical possession as there is no default in payment of license fees nor any violation of the terms and conditions thereof.

3. Mr. Bose, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a license holder to run a hotel and is having trade license and food safety license issued to him and refers to Annexure-2 series.

It is also submitted that the petitioner had made the deposits as required in terms of the license, hence, therefore, opposite party No.4 should be directed to renew the same without taking any coercive action.
Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel for opposite party No.4 refers to the counter affidavit and submits that the petitioner is a defaulter and there can be no renewal of license in his favour.

As per the affidavit, according to Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel, the petitioner was to make payment of license fee of Rs.2,000/- and deposited an amount of Rs. 50,000/- on 9th February,
2021 as against the outstanding dues of Rs. 1,26,000/- and it has become Rs.1,72,000/- payable till July, 2025 and therefore, no case is made out for renewal, hence, the writ petition should be dismissed.
4.

Considering the submissions as above and having regard to the fact that petitioner defaulted in making the payments and in the meantime, a decision has been taken to utilize the space for Shibasis Tripathy vs State Of Odisha And Others ....

1 construction of a bus stand, notwithstanding the fact that such a license was issued in 2015, the Court is of the view that on account of the serious default by him, renewal of the license is not to be directed.
Furthermore, the counter affidavit reveals that the site is earmarked for construction of a bus stand.

In any case, having regard to the submission of Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel for opposite party No.4, the Court reaches at a conclusion that opposite party Nos.2 to 4, under the above circumstances, cannot be directed to renew the agreement i.e. Annexure-1 as no case is made out and especially on account of the default of the petitioner.
5. Accordingly, it is ordered.
6. In the result, the writ petition stands dismissed.
As a consequence, the interim order dated 12th August, 2025 in I.A. No. 12790 of 2025 is hereby vacated as a result.
7. A copy of the order be supplied to Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel for opposite party No.4 for its onward intimation to the authority concerned.
